q: A cloud provider commits to 99.9% availability for a service that operates 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. What is the maximum downtime per year permitted under this commitment?
exp: Annual hours are 24 x 365 = 8,760, and 0.1% of 8,760 is 8.76 hours. The 52.6-minute figure corresponds to 99.99% availability.

q: A payment platform's SLA guarantees 99.95% availability measured over a 30-day month of continuous operation. What is the maximum allowable downtime in the month?
exp: A 30-day month has 720 hours; 0.05% x 720 = 0.36 hours, or 21.6 minutes. The 43.2-minute figure corresponds to 99.9% availability over the same month.

q: A server has a mean time between failures (MTBF) of 990 hours and a mean time to repair (MTTR) of 10 hours. What is its expected availability?
exp: Availability = MTBF / (MTBF + MTTR) = 990 / 1,000 = 99.0%. Dividing MTTR by MTBF (10/990) and subtracting from 100% gives the slightly different 98.99% trap.

q: An order-processing service requires a web server (99.0% available), an application server (99.5% available), and a database server (99.8% available), all of which must be running for the service to work. Assuming independent failures, what is the approximate availability of the service?
exp: Components in series multiply: 0.990 x 0.995 x 0.998 = about 0.983, or 98.3%. The service is less available than its weakest component, so 99.0% overstates it.

q: A company replaces a single application server that is 95% available with two identical servers running in parallel behind a load balancer, so the service is available if either server is running. Assuming independent failures and a perfectly reliable load balancer, what is the service's availability?
exp: Both servers must fail for an outage: probability 0.05 x 0.05 = 0.0025, so availability is 1 - 0.0025 = 99.75%. Multiplying 0.95 x 0.95 = 90.25% is the formula for components in series, not parallel.

q: An SLA promises 99.9% monthly availability for a $50,000 monthly fee, with a 10% service credit if availability falls below 99.9% but stays at or above 99.0%, and a 25% credit below 99.0%. In a 30-day month, the service was down for 2 hours. What credit is the customer owed?
exp: Availability = (720 - 2) / 720 = 99.72%, which is below 99.9% but above 99.0%, earning a 10% credit of $5,000. Assuming 2 hours falls below 99.0% would require more than 7.2 hours of downtime.

q: Under the Trust Services Criteria, which control most directly supports the availability criterion addressing the maintenance and monitoring of processing capacity to meet the entity's commitments (A1.1)?
choices: Monitoring CPU, memory, storage, and network utilization against thresholds, with capacity forecasts reviewed by management
A code of conduct signed annually by employees
exp: A1.1 addresses managing current capacity and forecasting future demand so the system can meet availability commitments. Access reviews and encryption support security and confidentiality rather than capacity.

q: A retailer's website crashed on Black Friday when traffic tripled, though no attack occurred. Which control would most likely have prevented the outage?
choices: Capacity planning with load testing and auto-scaling based on forecast peak demand
exp: Forecasting peak demand, load testing, and elastic scaling ensure systems can handle predictable spikes. Insurance might compensate for losses but does not keep the site running.

q: A company's online banking portal is flooded with traffic from thousands of compromised devices, making it unavailable to customers. Which control most directly mitigates this type of attack?
choices: A DDoS mitigation service that filters malicious traffic upstream, such as through a scrubbing center or content delivery network
exp: Distributed denial-of-service attacks overwhelm capacity, so they are best mitigated by upstream filtering and absorbing traffic at scale. MFA protects accounts but does nothing to stop volumetric traffic.

q: A review of a company's network architecture finds that all internet traffic passes through a single firewall with no failover. Which availability concept is most directly at issue?
exp: A component whose failure stops the entire service is a single point of failure, addressed through redundancy such as clustered firewalls. Defense in depth concerns layering security controls rather than eliminating unique dependencies.

q: Which Trust Services Criterion within the availability category is most directly supported by periodic testing of recovery plan procedures, including restoring backups at an alternate site?
exp: A1.3 requires the entity to test recovery plan procedures supporting system recovery to meet its objectives. CC6.1 addresses logical access, a common criterion for security.

q: A company's SOC 2 report covers processing integrity for its claims processing system. Which statement best describes processing integrity under the Trust Services Criteria?
choices: System processing is complete, valid, accurate, timely, and authorized to meet the entity's objectives
The system is protected against unauthorized access
Personal information is collected and used in accordance with the privacy notice
Information designated as confidential is protected
exp: Processing integrity addresses whether processing is complete, valid, accurate, timely, and authorized. Protection against unauthorized access is the security category, which is the common criteria baseline for every SOC 2.

q: A data entry clerk keys a customer number with two digits transposed. The system rejects it because the last digit, calculated from the other digits by an algorithm, no longer matches. Which input control is this?
exp: A check digit is derived mathematically from the other digits, so transpositions and most single-digit errors produce a mismatch. A limit check tests whether a value exceeds a predefined amount, not whether an identifier is valid.

q: A payroll system rejects any time card reporting more than 80 hours for a single week. Which input control is being applied?
exp: A limit check compares a value against a predetermined upper or lower bound. A field check tests that data is of the correct type, such as numeric characters only.

q: An accounts payable system compares the vendor number on each invoice against the vendor master file and rejects invoices from vendors not on the file. Which control is this?
exp: A validity check compares entered data against a list of valid values, such as authorized vendors in the master file. A reasonableness check tests whether a value is logical in relation to other data.

q: A payroll clerk adds the employee identification numbers on a batch of time cards and compares the sum with the total computed by the system after input. The sum has no meaning other than as a control. What is this total called?
exp: A hash total sums a field that has no arithmetic meaning, such as employee numbers, and detects lost, added, or altered records. A financial total sums a meaningful amount field like gross pay.

q: A batch of vendor invoices has a control sheet showing 250 documents totaling $125,400. After processing, the system reports 249 documents totaling $124,900. What do these batch controls most likely indicate?
choices: One invoice of $500 was not processed and should be investigated
The vendor master file contains an invalid vendor
exp: The record count is short by one (250 - 249) and the financial total is short by $500 ($125,400 - $124,900), suggesting one $500 invoice was lost or rejected. A duplicate would increase, not decrease, the totals.

q: A billing system rejects 3% of transactions for data errors and places them in a suspense file. Which additional control is most important to ensure processing integrity?
choices: Allowing any user to edit the suspense file
Monitoring the suspense file so rejected items are investigated, corrected, and resubmitted on a timely basis
Reporting rejected transactions to the external auditor only
exp: Error handling must ensure rejected items are tracked to resolution; otherwise valid transactions may never be recorded, impairing completeness. Deleting suspense items guarantees that legitimate revenue is lost.

q: Each nightly job in a multistep inventory processing run compares the record count and total quantity at the start of the step with those of the prior step's output. What type of control is this?
exp: Run-to-run totals verify that data is not lost or altered between processing steps, which is a processing control. Input controls validate data as it enters the system.

q: Two clerks simultaneously update the same customer's credit limit, and one update overwrites the other without warning. Which control would prevent this problem?
choices: Record locking or concurrency controls in the database
A limit check on the credit field
exp: Concurrency controls such as record locking prevent simultaneous updates from overwriting each other, preserving data integrity. A limit check validates the value but not the conflict between updates.

q: A sales order entry screen will not save an order until the customer number, product code, quantity, and ship-to address fields are all filled in. Which control is this?
exp: A completeness check ensures that all required fields contain data before a record is accepted. A sequence check verifies that items are in the expected order or that numbered documents have no gaps.

q: A company prints checks using prenumbered forms. At the end of each run, a clerk accounts for all check numbers, including voided ones, and investigates any gaps. Which control does this represent?
exp: Accounting for the numeric sequence of prenumbered documents detects missing, duplicate, or unauthorized items. A validity check compares values against a list of authorized entries.

q: Payroll registers containing employee salaries are automatically emailed to all department managers, including those who supervise none of the listed employees. Which processing integrity and confidentiality weakness is present?
choices: The suspense file is not monitored
Output is distributed beyond authorized recipients
exp: Output controls should ensure reports reach only authorized users who need them. Input validation and run-to-run totals address data accuracy rather than who receives the output.

q: A company's ERP system interfaces nightly with its bank to send payment files. Which control best ensures the files sent were completely and accurately received and processed?
choices: Reconciling the record counts and totals in the transmitted file with the bank's acknowledgment and the subsequent bank activity
Changing the bank portal password monthly
Printing the payment file for filing
exp: Reconciling control totals and acknowledgments confirms completeness and accuracy of the interface. Encryption protects confidentiality and integrity in transit but does not confirm the bank processed every payment.

q: A distribution company wants to ensure that its customer-facing order system defines what constitutes a valid order and how orders are processed, consistent with processing integrity criterion PI1.1. Which practice addresses this criterion?
choices: Documenting and communicating the system's data definitions and processing specifications, such as required fields, valid values, and processing rules
Requiring background checks for data entry clerks
exp: PI1.1 addresses obtaining or generating and communicating information about the objectives and specifications of processing, including data definitions. Encryption and penetration tests relate to security rather than processing specifications.

q: A subscription billing system occasionally charges customers twice when a network timeout causes the payment request to be resubmitted. Which control would best address this?
choices: Assigning unique transaction identifiers and rejecting duplicate submissions with the same identifier
Adding a limit check on the payment amount
exp: Duplicate detection using unique transaction IDs ensures each payment is processed only once even when requests are retried. A limit check would accept two charges that are each within the limit.

q: A company's data center has redundant power feeds, generators, raised floors, and temperature and humidity monitoring. Which availability criterion do these controls most directly support?
choices: A1.2, environmental protections and recovery infrastructure
exp: A1.2 addresses environmental protections, software, data backup processes, and recovery infrastructure. CC6.2 concerns registering and authorizing users, which is a logical access control.

q: A web application went down for six hours because a single expired disk license caused the storage array to stop accepting writes. Monitoring tools existed but alerts were sent to a mailbox no one reviewed. Which improvement would most directly reduce the risk of recurrence?
choices: Routing monitoring alerts to an on-call team with defined escalation procedures and response time targets
exp: Monitoring adds value only if alerts reach someone accountable for responding. A second tool sending alerts to the same unattended mailbox would not help.

q: A sales system checks whether the quantity ordered by a retail customer is consistent with that customer's historical ordering pattern and flags orders that are ten times the norm. Which control is this?
exp: A reasonableness check evaluates whether data is logical relative to other information, such as historical patterns. A field check only tests data type or format.

q: An insurer's claims system calculates benefits automatically. To verify processing accuracy as part of PI1.3, which control is most effective?
choices: Restricting physical access to the server room
Periodic backup of the claims database
Testing benefit calculation logic before deployment and periodically comparing a sample of system calculations with independent recalculations
Requiring claimants to use strong passwords
exp: PI1.3 addresses processing that is complete, accurate, and timely; validating calculation logic and periodically recalculating samples tests accuracy directly. Physical security and backups support other criteria.

q: An organization schedules maintenance windows for system patches on Sunday mornings and excludes them from the availability calculation in its customer SLA. What should a user entity understand about this arrangement?
choices: Scheduled maintenance always counts as unplanned downtime
The SLA guarantees the system will be available every minute of the year
Maintenance windows are prohibited under the Trust Services Criteria
The stated availability percentage may overstate the actual uptime experienced, so users should review SLA definitions and exclusions
exp: SLAs often exclude scheduled maintenance from availability calculations, so the headline percentage may not reflect total time the system is usable. The TSC do not prohibit maintenance windows; they require meeting commitments as defined.

q: A company wants its database to remain available if one server's power supply fails. Which hardware design best accomplishes this?
choices: Redundant, hot-swappable power supplies connected to separate power circuits
A UPS with five minutes of battery
exp: Redundant power supplies on separate circuits allow the server to keep running if one fails and to replace it without downtime. A larger single supply is still a single point of failure.

q: Which statement best explains why processing integrity is distinct from data integrity in a SOC 2 examination?
choices: Processing integrity applies only to financial systems, while data integrity applies to all systems

Processing integrity addresses whether the system's processing meets its objectives completely, validly, accurately, timely, and with authorization, not whether the underlying data was accurate when supplied by external sources
Processing integrity is a security criterion and is always included in SOC 2
Data integrity is a TSC category, while processing integrity is not
exp: The TSC note that processing integrity does not necessarily imply the data input from outside parties is correct; it focuses on the system processing that data as intended. Processing integrity is an optional category, not part of the security common criteria.

q: A company's e-commerce application writes order data to a primary database and a reporting database. Reports occasionally show orders that never appear in the primary database. Which control would best detect this problem?
choices: Automated daily reconciliation of record counts and totals between the primary and reporting databases, with exceptions investigated
Requiring complex passwords for report users
exp: Reconciliations between data stores detect inconsistencies such as phantom or missing records, supporting both processing and output integrity. Capacity and passwords do not address data consistency.

q: A cloud SaaS provider experienced three outages in a quarter, lasting 2 hours, 1.5 hours, and 30 minutes, during a 90-day quarter of continuous service. What was its availability for the quarter, rounded to two decimals?
exp: Total downtime is 2 + 1.5 + 0.5 = 4 hours out of 90 x 24 = 2,160 hours, so availability = 2,156 / 2,160 = 99.81%. Counting only the longest outage, or using a 30-day month as the base, produces the incorrect figures.

q: An application occasionally posts transactions with a date in the following year because users mistype the year. Which input control would best prevent this?
choices: A range check limiting transaction dates to the current open accounting period
A hash total of transaction dates
A sequence check on invoice numbers
A check digit on the customer number
exp: A range check enforces upper and lower bounds, such as dates within the open period. A hash total could detect changes in a batch, but would not prevent a keyed future date.

q: A company's availability commitments state that customer data will be recoverable to within one hour of any failure. Which control most directly supports meeting this commitment?
choices: Continuous or at least hourly replication or backup of customer data, with monitoring of job success
Annual review of the backup policy
Restricting access to the backup room
exp: A one-hour recovery point commitment requires capturing data at least hourly and confirming those jobs succeed. Weekly backups would allow up to a week of data loss.

q: A company archives processed loan records to a data warehouse used for regulatory reporting. Which control most directly supports the processing integrity criterion that stored data be maintained completely and accurately over time (PI1.5)?
choices: Limiting the number of reports users can run each day
Requiring loan officers to complete privacy training
Periodic integrity checks, such as comparing stored record counts and checksums with source totals, and restricting changes to archived records
Encrypting loan records while they are transmitted to the warehouse
exp: PI1.5 addresses storing inputs, items in processing, and outputs completely, accurately, and timely, which integrity checks and change restrictions on stored data support. Encryption in transit protects data on the way in but does not show that the stored data remains complete and unaltered.
